text:
maria: Hey — running `terraform plan` for staging after a manual kubectl import and the plan is showing the ServiceAccount will be recreated (diff shows ownerReferences/annotations removed). Also apply is stuck because the remote state lock in S3 looks held. Who can help force-unlock + reimport so we don't accidentally recreate the SA?

ops_jessie: I can look. Do you have the lock ID and the exact plan snippet?

maria: Lock ID from the provider error: `5f3b2a0c-locked-by-ci` (sounds like a dead CI run). Plan snippet:```~ kubernetes_service_account.ingress
  metadata.0.annotations: {
    "owner" => "redwood-manifest" -> null
  }
  # forces replacement because owner removed
```

samir: fyi if ownerAnnotations are managed by helm upstream then terraform will always try to change it after import. Two things we can do: (1) import the resource and then update the TF state to match the cluster, or (2) add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }` for the SA so TF stops fighting helm.

maria: option (1) preferred for now — we want TF to own it in staging.

ops_jessie: OK steps I'd follow:```bash
# force unlock (only if no active apply)
terraform force-unlock 5f3b2a0c-locked-by-ci
# import resource to the same address as in config
terraform import module.k8s.kubernetes_service_account.ingress default/ingress-sa
# refresh and replan
terraform refresh -target=module.k8s.kubernetes_service_account.ingress
terraform plan -target=module.k8s.kubernetes_service_account.ingress
```

samir: +1. Also check the CI pipeline: if that lock was from a running job we could race. Maybe pause the CI apply queue for staging briefly.

maria: CI job definitely died (timeout). I've paused the staging apply queue in the console.

terra-bot: Lock checker: no active locks found on backend after 2m. Last lock ID record: `5f3b2a0c-locked-by-ci` at 2024-05-02T03:12:10Z.

ops_jessie: I'm going to run `force-unlock` now. Will post outputs.

maria: thanks. Also the SA has an extra `owner` annotation on the cluster that TF config doesn't include — import should make plan happy but if plan still shows replace we can add a minimal `ignore_changes` for that single key instead of all annotations.

ops_jessie: force-unlock complete: `Force-unlock succeeded: 5f3b2a0c-locked-by-ci`. Running import...

ops_jessie: import succeeded: `Imported kubernetes_service_account.ingress (ID: default/ingress-sa)`. Running `terraform plan -target=module.k8s.kubernetes_service_account.ingress` now.

samir: nice — if plan still shows replace paste the diff here. Might be a small annotation mismatch.

ops_jessie: plan result: no replacement, only minor annotation drift (owner key present in state now). Looks safe.

maria: amazing, thanks both. I'll unpause CI in 10m and run a full staging apply then.

deploy-bot: reminder: scheduled staging apply at 2024-05-02T04:00:00Z canceled by maria (:white_check_mark:).

maria: leaving a note in the PR: imported SA in state, forced unlock, verified plan no longer recreates resource. We'll follow up with a short RFC to decide whether to manage owner annotation from TF or leave it to helm. :memo:

ops_jessie: FYI added `// ops: imported to state 2024-05-02` to the terraform module comments.

maria: resolving — thanks all :raised_hands:
